messages:
maya (eng-platform): Heads-up — AcmeCorp asked for an ephemeral burst override to route their org traffic to the high-priority pool for a 2h demo. Need proposal for API + console flow, audit fields, and safety checks. Who can own?

sam (eng-runtime): We already have a runtime tag `burst=true` but org-level overrides are disabled. Safety items: token-scoped rate limits, automatic model fallback, per-override cost cap, and isolation so other tenants can't slip in.

adele (product): UX idea — a console modal to request an override with fields: org, duration, reason, cost-limit, approver, and a pre-flight estimate. Show telemetry link and a revoke button. Keep it one-click for enterprise admins but require approval for > $X/day.

kevin (security): Agree on approval gate. Add these constraints: HMAC-signed approval token for any manual approve, KMS-backed audit note storage, header-mangling to strip internal routing headers from downstream logs, and mandatory security sign-off if cost_limit exceeds threshold. Also record approver identity and MFA status.

ops-bot: [system] Reminder: ephemeral override created by linda for org=AcmeCorp will expire in 2h. Will send notice 15m before expiry. :bell:

maya (eng-platform): Proposal sketch for the API endpoint:

```
POST /api/v1/overrides/ephemeral
{
  "org_id": "acmecorp",
  "duration_seconds": 7200,
  "cost_limit_cents": 500000, // $5k
  "reason": "Sales demo - 2025-06-12",
  "requester": "linda",
  "approver": "adele",
  "hmac": "<signed-token>"
}
```

Approval flow idea: requests go to product for initial approve; if cost_limit > threshold then require security sign-off; otherwise auto-approve after 10m if no denies. All actions must write audit events.

sam (eng-runtime): Runtime can add `override_id` and TTL to routing decisions and tag all emitted traces with `override.active=true` + `override.id`. We'll expose metrics: `override.active_count`, `override.estimated_cost`, and `override.rollback_count`. Also ensure batching policy treats burst pool as isolated (no cross-tenant batching).

linda (solutions): Sales note — Acme accepts a cost cap and wants a fast path in the console (enterprise admin bypass). They also asked for an exportable audit CSV showing request/approve/revoke history.

adele (product): Console UX details: show an 'Override history' table, TTL slider (15m-24h), reason field with markdown, pre-flight simulation that shows estimated token spend by model variant, and a revoke button that triggers immediate rollback + notification.

kevin (security): Audit requirements: before/after routing decisions, headers, approver identity, approve HMAC, and retention 1y. Also require alerting if active override breaches the cost_limit by >5%.

maya (eng-platform): OK — next steps: I'll draft a short playbook + RFC including API schema, approval flow, telemetry fields, and console mocks. Can we agree on the HMAC approve + key telemetry fields?

sam (eng-runtime): :thumbsup: runtime on board. We'll implement rollback hooks and add a simulator endpoint to estimate cost for given burst size.

ci-bot: [ci] Ticket created: PLT-1234 — ephemeral override API + console work. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/PLT-1234

maya (eng-platform): thanks — I'll open the RFC and ping @kevin for the security gate details.

kevin (security): Ping acknowledged. I'll add the HMAC spec and approval thresholds to the RFC.

adele (product): I'll sketch the modal mock and link it to PLT-1234.

linda (solutions): I'll prep the customer-facing FAQ for Acme about cost caps and revocation.

maya (eng-platform): Great. If no objections I'll start the RFC tomorrow and attach a minimal JSON schema and a console mock.

sam (eng-runtime): No objections from runtime. Please include test harness for simulation and a stress test plan.

maya (eng-platform): cool — closing thread for now. Will update when RFC is up. :white_check_mark:
